top.headline: Trump's Midterm Interference Push Is Collapsing Under Its Own Numbers, Elections Expert Says
top.blurb: Elections expert David Becker says Trump's hunt for 'noncitizen voters' is collapsing under its own numbers: 28 arrests out of 23 million California voters, a Nevada list of 16,000 names that shrank to 185 — all citizens — and 27 straight court losses, nine before Trump-appointed judges. A federal court has already blocked ICE's armed door-knocking through Election Day.

top.headline: AIPAC Isn't Retreating From the Midterms. It's Just Harder to See.
top.blurb: AIPAC says it's dropping direct candidate endorsements after Gaza made its brand toxic with voters, but an Intercept analysis finds it simply rerouted the money: its super PAC funneled $13.1 million through pop-up committees, with names like 'Chicago Progressive Partnership,' that attacked primary candidates who rejected Israel-lobby money, then quietly folded.

top.headline: Regulators and Senators Escalate Scrutiny of DraftKings After ProPublica's VIP Reporting
top.blurb: After ProPublica found DraftKings kept a reporter who bet like a problem gambler in VIP status, Louisiana regulators denied the company's license renewal, Ohio proposed barring marketing for 48 hours after bettors opt into safeguards, and three Senate Democrats demanded sportsbooks disclose how much revenue comes from their most compulsive users.

top.headline: Instagram Takedowns in India Surged Sevenfold in October, Hitting Journalists Covering the SIR
top.blurb: A Newslaundry investigation counts 351 Meta, X, Reddit and YouTube content or account restrictions in India this October, nearly seven times July's rate. Journalist Raghav Trivedi's Instagram reach collapsed from 100 million to 30 million after repeated takedowns, coinciding with protests over the Election Commission's special intensive revision of voter rolls.

top.headline: Supreme Court Orders Election Commission to Act on Bulk Voter-Deletion Filings in UP's SIR
top.blurb: The Supreme Court directed the Election Commission to act against bulk Form 7 filings used to delete voters from Uttar Pradesh's rolls, after petitioners showed 32 deletion applications filed against one community in a single constituency, two of them signed by booth-level officers themselves.

top.headline: India's Extreme Poverty Falls to 2.6%, but Top Earners Now Make 13 Times the Bottom Decile
top.blurb: A World Bank brief finds India's extreme poverty rate has fallen to 2.6% from 27.1% in 2011, lifting nearly 50 crore people out of poverty, even as the top 10% of workers now earn 13 times the bottom decile and rural youth unemployment keeps climbing.

top.headline: Tankers Hit by Mines in Strait of Hormuz as Trump Says Iran War Will 'Wrap Up Soon'
top.blurb: Iran's Revolutionary Guards said four oil tankers caught fire after striking mines in the Strait of Hormuz, and a drone reportedly targeted Riyadh, as the eight-month US-Israel-Iran war escalated further. Trump said the conflict would 'wrap up soon,' even as Iran's foreign minister threatened an 'earth-shattering' retaliatory strike if attacked again.

top.headline: Poland Suspends Top Judge, Deploys Police, as President Turns Plane Around Mid-Flight
top.blurb: Poland suspended Constitutional Tribunal president Bogdan Swieczkowski, a PiS appointee accused of blocking parliament's judicial picks for six months to keep the court paralysed, triggering protests and a police deployment outside the Warsaw court. President Karol Nawrocki, a PiS ally, turned his plane around mid-flight, declaring the president 'must be in Poland.'

top.headline: G20 Scraps Group Photo as Europeans Refuse to Stand Beside Russia's Lavrov
top.blurb: The US cancelled the G20 foreign ministers' traditional group photo after European officials refused to be pictured beside sanctioned Russian minister Sergey Lavrov, and no joint statement will be issued at all — a sign, one diplomat said, that the G20 'is no longer effectively a forum' for consensus amid splits over Ukraine and Iran.

top.headline: South Africa's Centurions Set Australia 288 to Win Deciding Test on Final Day
top.blurb: Ryan Rickelton and Wiaan Mulder both scored centuries in a defiant 154-run stand to set Australia 288 to win the deciding Test of a series level at 1-1, with Starc, Cummins and Lyon sharing the wickets on a worn Newlands pitch as the series heads into its final day.

top.headline: Rashid Khan Becomes First Bowler to 200 T20I Wickets in Afghanistan's Series-Sealing Win
top.blurb: Rashid Khan became the first bowler to take 200 T20I wickets, reaching the milestone in his 120th international as Afghanistan beat Zimbabwe by 19 runs to seal an unassailable series lead, built on Azmatullah Omarzai's maiden T20I century and a record 142-run stand after Afghanistan had slumped to 5 for 4.

top.headline: 'Wicker' Review: Olivia Colman Marries a Willow Man in an Outlandish Fairy Tale Romance
top.blurb: In this genre-bending fairy tale, Olivia Colman's shunned fisherwoman commissions a willow-and-wicker husband, played by Alexander Skarsgård, from the village's basket weaver, scandalising the wives of duller men. Critic Nandini Ramnath calls it one of the most outlandish, enchanting odd-couple romances in recent memory, carried by striking cinematography and Colman's heartbreaking comic performance.

top.headline: Archive of Our Own Goes Dark for Up to a Month After a 'Security Incident,' Scattering Fandom
top.blurb: Archive of Our Own, the volunteer-run fanfiction site with millions of users, went dark for what could be a month after what its nonprofit operator now says was a security incident, scattering writers to Wattpad, FanFiction.net and Space Battles mid-Kinktober. Readers say the disruption revealed how much of the site's appeal was never just storage, but its shared tagging system and comments.

bengal.headline: Bengal Orders Forensic Audit of Swasthya Sathi After Scheme Can't Find 30-40 Lakh Beneficiaries
bengal.blurb: Bengal's health minister ordered a forensic audit of the Swasthya Sathi health scheme after verification failed to locate 30-40 lakh listed beneficiaries, alleging fake cards, forged signatures and fictitious hospitals worth up to ₹30,000 crore.

bengal.headline: Bengal Plans a State School of Magic, Chaired by P.C. Sorcar (Junior)
bengal.blurb: Bengal's government formed an advisory committee, chaired by magician P.C. Sorcar (Junior), to plan a state school and museum devoted to magic and illusion, fulfilling a research centre Sorcar has sought for years.

bengal.headline: CM Adhikari Vows to Seize 'Grabbed' Land for SC/ST Families, Warns of More Arrests
bengal.blurb: At a Baruipur rally, Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari pledged to seize illegally occupied land for distribution to Scheduled Caste and Tribe families, while warning Mamata and Abhishek Banerjee that more arrests over alleged corruption were coming 'soon.'

travel.headline: Mexico's Bread of the Dead Kneads Together Indigenous and Catholic Traditions
travel.blurb: Pan de muerto, the sweet bread baked for Día de los Muertos altars, blends Indigenous Mexican ritual with imported Catholic symbolism, its shape and sugar-skull topping reworking older Aztec offerings to the dead into a tradition now sold on street corners nationwide.

travel.headline: Aztec Planting Techniques and Crocodiles Are Reviving Mexico's Mangroves
travel.blurb: A Mexican nonprofit is reviving Veracruz's mangroves by planting seedlings on raised, Aztec-style soil mounds and releasing juvenile crocodiles believed to keep tidal channels clear, reaching 80% canopy cover on its original plot within eight years.

happy.headline: After 150 Years of Digging at Troy, Archaeologists Finally Found Its Music
happy.blurb: Archaeologists at Troy have found the site's first musical instrument in 150 years of excavation: a bone flute from around the eighth century B.C.E., roughly when Homer is thought to have composed the Iliad and the Odyssey. Composer Ludwig Göransson later used a replica of a similar ancient instrument for the sirens' song in Christopher Nolan's Odyssey — an echo, 2,800 years on, of music this same ground once made.

tech_top.headline: North Korean Hackers Blamed for Record $6.3 Billion Binance Breach
tech_top.pm_note: The breach traced back to one engineer's compromised laptop reaching a production service container — a reminder that your attack surface is every employee's device, not just your servers.
tech_top.blurb: Blockchain forensics firms TRM Labs and Elliptic have attributed the record $6.3 billion theft from Binance's wallets to North Korea's TraderTraitor group, the same cell blamed for 2025's $1.4 billion Bybit hack. About half the stolen funds have been frozen by Tether, Circle and other partners; Binance says it found no evidence its private keys leaked.

tech_top.headline: Cracks Are Emerging in the AI Spending Boom
tech_top.pm_note: Negative free cash flow at three of the four hyperscalers, even as cloud revenue keeps growing, is the clearest sign yet that AI infrastructure bets are now a balance-sheet risk, not just a growth story.
tech_top.blurb: Alphabet, Amazon and Meta all posted negative free cash flow last quarter despite a combined $740 billion capex plan, and Alphabet's stock had its worst day on record, erasing $500 billion in value. The five biggest AI spenders have raised $326 billion in debt this year, roughly triple 2025's pace, to keep funding the buildout.

tech_top.headline: A Hardcoded Password in Applebee's App Exposed Its 8.5 Million Rewards Members
tech_top.pm_note: A password baked into a shipped mobile app, found by a researcher using AI to scan the decompiled code, is a reminder that 'it's just a mobile app' is exactly the assumption that leaves credentials sitting in plain text.
tech_top.blurb: A researcher found a hardcoded database password inside Applebee's Android app that exposed names, birth dates, phone numbers and login IP addresses for its 8.5 million-member rewards program. Parent company Dine Brands fixed the flaw after TechCrunch's report but won't say how long the credential was exposed or whether it will notify regulators.

tech_101.text: The cash a company has left after operating expenses and capital spending — the number investors are now watching anxiously as Alphabet, Amazon and Meta all post negative figures despite surging AI revenue, because it measures whether the spending is sustainable, not just whether the business is growing.

A password or key written directly into an app's code rather than stored in a secure backend system. Anyone who has the app can extract it, which is how a researcher turned Applebee's Android app into a password for its entire customer database.

science.headline: Chemists Build a Tattoo Ink That Vanishes on Command
science.blurb: Chemists led by Carson Bruns at the University of Colorado Boulder built a photochromic tattoo ink that switches on with a few seconds of UV light and off under bright white light, now stable enough for months of use and over 10,000 cycles. Bruns, who has tested hundreds of the tattoos on himself, hopes eventually to use them as medical markers that vanish once no longer needed.

science.headline: Astronauts Complete Seven-Hour Spacewalk to Upgrade the Space Station's Power
science.blurb: NASA's Anil Menon and Canadian astronaut Joshua Kutryk spent just over seven hours installing the seventh of eight new roll-out solar arrays on the International Space Station, part of an upgrade expected to boost the station's power by up to 30%. A second spacewalk on November 5 will fit the final array and complete the project.

philosophy.headline: Why Real Intelligence Has to Be More Than Optimisation
philosophy.blurb: Philosopher Sasha Mudd argues that defining intelligence as optimisation, a fair description of most AI, quietly smuggles in Hume's claim that reason only serves our existing ends. Drawing on Kant, she argues real intelligence can judge which ends are worth pursuing at all, and warns that treating 'alignment' as purely technical lets a society's actual goals, like engagement or growth, escape scrutiny entirely.

philosophy.headline: Why We Should Heed Barbara Ward's Vision of Planetary Justice
philosophy.blurb: Economist Barbara Ward, who coined the term 'sustainable development' in the 1970s, argued that prosperity, equality and the environment had to be governed together at a planetary scale, not fought over nation by nation. Historian Or Rosenboim argues her vision anticipated today's linked crises, though her Western-centric, Christian framing needed the postcolonial correction she herself moved toward late in life.

philosophy.headline: In Praise of the Dilettante
philosophy.blurb: Jay Miller defends the dilettante, someone who pursues many interests for delight rather than career or credentials, against the modern cult of specialisation, tracing the insult back to Goethe and Schiller's 1799 essay on dilettantism. He argues a life of rotating passions, like a cosmopolitan who travels between crafts without settling in any one, can be as meaningful as a life built around a single vocation.

philosophy_101.text: In Kant's ethics, being governed by ends imposed from outside yourself, such as a market signal or an algorithm's prediction, rather than ones you've reasoned your way to and would endorse. Today's essay on AI and intelligence borrows the term to describe what's at stake in letting optimisation define our goals for us.

Someone who pursues a craft or interest for pleasure rather than profession or credential — a term that curdled from a neutral Baroque-Italian label into an insult, which today's essay tries to reclaim as a form of freedom rather than a lack of seriousness.
